top: Alabama Voice Of Teachers For Education
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Democrat from Montgomery. Former English teacher at Rye Country Day School in New York and community organizer. Served in the Alabama House (District 78) from 2018 to 2021. Has held Alabama Senate District 26 since winning a 2021 special election.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Hatcher grew up, though Wikipedia calls Montgomery his hometown. We found no sponsored bills, public statements or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2021, 2022 or 2026, and the pages we had list no campaign website or policy platform. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia says he was born in Montgomery, and Wikipedia says he moved back to his hometown in about 2015 after studying in Atlanta and teaching in New York, so the record shows roughly 11 years of adult residence in Alabama. · Money: 16% of money from District 26 ZIP codes after leaving out land and development money (24% before)

qual.background: Alabama House member for District 78 from 2018 to 2021, then Alabama Senate member for District 26 from March 2021 to the present; earlier worked as an English teacher and community organizer.
qual.why: More than five years of prior legislative service in both chambers puts him in the high band for writing law and the state budget; his teaching and organizing work is unrelated to the office and adds little.
